office_does: The assessor sets the assessed values that property taxes are based on and runs exemption programs such as the senior citizen and disabled persons exemption.
race_blurb: Bruce Walker, assessor since his 2002 election and seeking a seventh term, faces his first opponent in 24 years, Ocean Park accountant Jeff Phelan, who promises to lower property taxes. Both state no party preference; Walker led the primary 5,011 to 3,366.

candidates.summary: Incumbent assessor, first elected in 2002, and former title officer; filed no voters' guide statement.
highlights: First elected in 2002; ran unopposed in 2022 [S2][S5]
His office's columns explain the expanded 2026 senior and disabled exemptions [S3][S4]
Notes that exempted taxes shift to other property owners in the district [S3]

candidates.summary: Ocean Park resident with a utility accounting background, running to 'exempt, reduce, or remove' property taxes.
highlights: Says he 'will exempt, reduce, or remove your property taxes where possible' [S1]
Calls for 'new blood' after the incumbent's 20-plus years [S1]
Pledges to cut costs without affecting staff [S1]
The Chinook Observer reported his Facebook posts attacking the Chinook Indian Nation and Democrats [S2]

experience.basis: First-time candidate running explicitly on 'new blood' against a long-tenured incumbent.

taxes.basis: Frames his candidacy around reducing property taxes on fixed-income owners.

spending.basis: Pledges to streamline processes and reduce costs.
